mainTopic: Do the bitter waters test a סוטה who has witnesses? The burned מנחה, רב פפא's גזירה, and a ברייתא supporting רב ששת
overview: The amud opens with a challenge to רב ששת, who ruled that the bitter waters do not test a סוטה when there are witnesses to her sin. A משנה says that if witnesses come against her, her מנחה is burned. That means it was truly holy, so it seems she was fit for the test after all. רב יהודה מדיסקרתא answers that the witnesses saw a new sin in the עזרה, after the מנחה was made holy. רב משרשיא and רב אשי then argue over how she could sin there. רב פפא gives a different answer: by Torah law the מנחה is חולין, but the רבנן ordered it burned so people won't think things can leave a כלי שרת and become ordinary. רב מרי challenges this from a ברייתא that says the מנחה becomes חולין when the witnesses are found to be זוממין. The גמרא answers that the story of עדים זוממין becomes public, so no one will be misled. Next, a ברייתא supports רב ששת by learning from וטהורה היא that three kinds of women who survive the water do not get its blessing. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a question on רבי שמעון, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about women whose מנחה is burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes part of a משנה. It says that a woman who admits she is טמאה, and a woman against whom witnesses testify, both have their מנחה burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who says 'I am טמאה,' and a woman about whom witnesses came and said that she is טמאה, have their מנחה burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from a משנה. It will use this line as the base for a challenge in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases where the סוטה's מנחה is burned instead of being offered or returned to normal use. Burning tells us the flour had already become fully holy. The next steps ask how that could be true in the case of witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am impure,' meaning she admits she was unfaithful
Witnesses
Meal-offering; the סוטה brings a barley offering
Is burned (it may not be eaten)

phrases.english: One who says: 'I am defiled,'
and one about whom witnesses came that she is defiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֶרֶת טְמֵאָה אֲנִי וְשֶׁבָּאוּ לָהּ עֵדִים שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes a משנה as the basis for a challenge to רב ששת's ruling that the waters do not test a סוטה when there are witnesses to her guilt
steps.raayaObject: Whether מים בודקין אותה when there are witnesses
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing women whose מנחה is burned
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that אין המים בודקין אותה when there are witnesses to her guilt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says this woman's מנחה is burned, which implies it was validly made holy. Steps 2–4 show this fits only if the waters test her even when witnesses exist.

steps.title: When did the witnesses come? Not before the מנחה became holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the witnesses testified. It rules out 'before the מנחה was made holy,' because then the flour would just go back to being חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did the witnesses come? If you say before the מנחה was made holy, it should simply go out to חולין and not be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the witnesses arrived. It rejects the first option, the earlier time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה becomes fully holy only once it is put into a כלי שרת. If the witnesses came before that point, the test is no longer needed. The flour would then go back to ordinary use, not be burned. So the משנה must be talking about witnesses who came later.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say (this opens a possibility that is about to be rejected)
Before it becomes holy (in the כלי שרת)
It should go out to ordinary, non-holy status

phrases.english: Where witnesses came, when did they come?
If we say before it was sanctified,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מנחה, which becomes holy when it is placed in a holy Temple vessel.

phrases.english: it should go out to non-sacred status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down the case of witnesses in the quoted משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what point did the witnesses testify: before or after the מנחה was made holy?

steps.title: It must be after, which makes sense if the waters still test her
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses must have come after the מנחה was made holy. If the waters test her even when there are witnesses, the מנחה was properly made holy, and that is why it is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was after the מנחה was made holy. Granted, if you say the waters test her even when there are witnesses, then she was fit to bring an offering. When the מנחה was made holy at the start, it was made holy properly. That is why her מנחה is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles that the witnesses came after the מנחה was made holy. It then shows that the burning fits well with one side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that was properly made holy cannot go back to חולין, so it has to be burned. If the waters test her even when witnesses exist, she was a proper candidate for the offering. Her flour was then validly made holy, and burning is exactly right. This is the 'easy' side, and it sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: After it was made holy
It works well if you say
The bitter waters test her
Fit to be made holy and offered
It was properly made holy

phrases.english: Rather, it was after it was sanctified.
Granted, if you say
the water evaluates her,
phrases.notes: He means the waters test her even though there are witnesses who know she sinned.

phrases.english: evidently it is fit to be sanctified and offered,
and when it was sanctified at the outset, it was properly sanctified,
and because of that her meal-offering is burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְבָתַר דִּקְדוּשׁ אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of 'when' and shows how the משנה fits the view that the waters do test her
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses came after the מנחה was made holy. This fits well if the waters test her despite the witnesses.

steps.title: If the waters do not test her, the מנחה should go back to חולין
steps.stepSummary: If the waters do not test her when there are witnesses, the מנחה was made holy by mistake from the start. It should go back to חולין, not be burned. This is a challenge against that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the waters do not test her when there are witnesses, then it turns out, looking back, that when the מנחה was made holy it was made holy by mistake. So it should go out to חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that אין המים בודקין אותה when witnesses exist. Under that view, the משנה's ruling to burn the מנחה makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses exist, then under this view the woman was never fit for the test. Her מנחה should never have been made holy. Holiness given by mistake does not take effect, so the flour should become ordinary again. Yet the משנה says to burn it, which shows it was truly holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The waters do not test her (when there are witnesses)
It becomes clear, looking back, what was true all along
By mistake

steps.whatToRemember: A burned מנחה means it was truly holy. That fits only if the waters test her even when witnesses exist. If they do not, the flour was made holy by mistake and should return to חולין.
steps.confusionAlert: The witnesses came only AFTER the flour was made holy. But if the waters do not test such a woman, she was never fit in the first place, because the witnesses already knew about her. So looking back, the holiness was a mistake from the very start.

phrases.english: But if you say
the water does not evaluate her,
let the matter be revealed retroactively
that when it was sanctified at the outset, it was sanctified in error,
and let it go out to non-sacred status!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין הַמַּיִם בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the other side of the argument: under the opposing view, the משנה's ruling fails
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's view that the waters do not test a סוטה when there are witnesses to her guilt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view, the מנחה was made holy by mistake and should go back to חולין. Yet the משנה rules that it is burned.

steps.title: She sinned in the courtyard after the offering was made holy
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא explains that the witnesses saw her sin in the עזרה, after the מנחה was already properly made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה from דיסקרתא said: The case is where she committed adultery in the Temple courtyard. When the מנחה was made holy at the start, it was made holy properly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from step 4 by changing the case. The witnesses are not talking about the first sin. They saw a new sin that happened in the עזרה, after the מנחה was already made holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 4 was that the מנחה had been made holy by mistake. רב יהודה says there was no mistake: when it was made holy, she really was supposed to drink. The new sin came later, so the מנחה was properly holy and must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
At the start, from the beginning
Properly, well
Was made holy

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda from Diskarta said:
For example, where she committed adultery in the Temple courtyard,
phrases.notes: This is a new sin, after the מנחה was made holy. The witnesses are talking about this one, not the first one.

phrases.english: for when it was made holy at the start, it was made holy properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by redefining which sin the witnesses saw.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses testify about the original sin, so the מנחה was made holy by mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witnesses testify about a later sin in the עזרה, so the מנחה was made holy properly and is burned.

steps.title: But young priests escort her the whole time
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא challenges the idea that she could sin in the עזרה, since young כהנים stay with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objects: But don't young כהנים escort her?
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא attacks רב יהודה's case. How could she sin in the עזרה if young כהנים are with her the whole time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's answer depends on her having a chance to sin in the עזרה. If she is always watched, that case seems impossible, and the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, challenges it
Young כהנים, literally 'blossoms of the priesthood'
Escort, accompany

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya objects to this:
But don't young priests accompany her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the case in step 5 could really happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's case of a sin in the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is always escorted by young כהנים, so she has no chance to sin there.

steps.title: She sinned with the young priests themselves
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the escorts themselves were the ones she sinned with.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where she committed adultery with the young כהנים themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה. Having escorts does not stop the sin if the escorts are the ones she sinned with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the escorts would protect her. This answer points out that the escorts themselves could be part of the sin, so רב יהודה's case still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves
That she committed adultery

phrases.english: Where she committed adultery with the young priests themselves.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The escorts make a sin in the עזרה impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: She sinned with the escorts themselves.

steps.title: She went off alone to relieve herself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another way she could sin despite the escorts: they let her go alone to relieve herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where she needed to relieve herself. Do the young כהנים keep her locked in a cell?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to רב משרשיא's challenge. The escorts do not watch her every single moment, for example when she goes to relieve herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying the escorts were the sinners, רב אשי says there were gaps in the watching. That gives her a chance to sin with someone else, so רב יהודה's case still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: She needed to relieve herself
Is that to say? (a rhetorical question)
A cell or enclosed room
Hold, keep

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
For example, where she needed to relieve herself,
phrases.notes: The escorts let her go off privately, and she sinned there.

phrases.english: for is that to say the young priests
hold her in a cell?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּצְרְכָה לִנְקָבֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to רב משרשיא's challenge, in place of step 7.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are moments she is out of their sight, so she could sin with others.

steps.title: Burned only because of a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא keeps the original case. By Torah law the מנחה is חולין, but the רבנן made it holy so people won't think things can leave a כלי שרת and become ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Really, it is as we said at first. And what you said, that it should go out to חולין, is true. But it is burned because of the רבנן, as a decree, so people won't say: you can take things out of a כלי שרת and make them ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a whole new answer to step 4. He agrees the witnesses are about the original sin and that by Torah law the מנחה is חולין. Still, the רבנן decreed that it be treated as holy and burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה changed the case. רב פפא keeps the case and changes the reason. The burning is not a Torah rule but a rabbinic גזירה. Onlookers saw the מנחה go into a כלי שרת and don't know it was a mistake, so they might learn that holy things can just become ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the original explanation)
By rabbinic law
A protective rabbinic decree
Holy Temple service vessels
Ordinary, not holy

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain why the מנחה is burned. One is that the witnesses saw a later sin, so the מנחה was truly holy (רב יהודה, defended against רב משרשיא's challenge in two ways). The other is that by Torah law it is חולין, but the רבנן decreed burning so no one thinks things can leave a כלי שרת and become ordinary (רב פפא).
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not say the מנחה is truly holy by Torah law. He agrees it is חולין מדאורייתא; the burning is only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Actually, it is as we said initially,
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses are about the original sin, the case from step 3.

phrases.english: and that which you said, let it go out to non-sacred status,
it is holy by rabbinic law, a decree lest people say:
one may take out from a service vessel to non-sacred status.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְאָמְרִינַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the קשיא of step 4, keeping the original case instead of using רב יהודה's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מנחה was made holy by mistake, it should go back to חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it is חולין, but a rabbinic גזירה requires burning so people won't think things can leave a כלי שרת and become ordinary.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the burning of the מנחה can fit even the view that the waters do not test her when there are witnesses.

steps.title: רב מרי opens his challenge with a ברייתא about an impure מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי begins quoting a ברייתא. Its first rule: if the סוטה's מנחה became impure before it was put in a כלי שרת, it is redeemed. If it became impure after, it is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי objects: If her meal-offering became impure before it was made holy in a vessel, it is like all meal-offerings and is redeemed. If it became impure after it was made holy in a vessel, it is like all meal-offerings and is burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי starts an objection against רב פפא by quoting a ברייתא. This first part is setting up the background; the real attack comes at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first shows that the סוטה's מנחה follows the normal rules of every מנחה. Before a כלי שרת it can still be redeemed. After a כלי שרת it is fully holy and must be burned if it becomes impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
Became ritually impure
Was made holy by being put in a כלי שרת (Temple service vessel)
It is redeemed, so its holiness is moved off it
It must be burned

phrases.english: Rav Mari raises an objection:
phrases.notes: His objection is aimed at רב פפא's answer from the step just before.

phrases.english: If her meal-offering became impure
before it was made holy in a vessel
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is redeemed.
If it was after it was made holy in a vessel
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against רב פפא's answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the רבנן keep the מנחה holy once it was in a כלי שרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This opening part only lays the groundwork. The ברייתא's final clause will show a sanctified מנחה becoming חולין.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: what happens if the husband or wife dies
steps.stepSummary: If the קומץ was made holy but not yet offered when the husband or wife died, the מנחה is burned. If the קומץ was already offered, the leftovers are eaten, because the מנחה already did its job of atoning for the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the handful was made holy and he did not manage to offer it before the husband or wife died, it is like all meal-offerings and is burned. If the handful was offered and he did not manage to eat the leftovers before the husband or wife died, it is like all meal-offerings and is eaten. It came at the start because of a doubt, and it atoned for that doubt and is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going, still giving background before the key line. It explains what happens to the מנחה if the husband or wife dies at different stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the קומץ is offered, the מנחה is still holy but no longer needed, so it is burned. Once the קומץ is offered, the מנחה has already atoned for the doubt about her. So the leftovers stay fine to eat even though she will never drink the water.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from the מנחה and offered on the מזבח
The leftovers of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
Managed in time
It atoned for her doubt

phrases.english: If the handful was made holy,
and he did not manage to offer it

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמֵּת הוּא אוֹ עַד שֶׁמֵּתָה הִיא
phrases.english: before he died or before she died
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is burned.
If the handful was offered
and he did not manage to eat the leftovers

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁמֵּת הוּא אוֹ עַד שֶׁמֵּתָה הִיא
phrases.english: before he died or before she died
it is like all meal-offerings, and it is eaten.
For it came at the start because of a doubt,
it atoned for its doubt and went on its way.
phrases.notes: Literally 'and went away': its job was finished once the קומץ was offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא that רב מרי brought in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband or wife dies before the קומץ is offered, the מנחה is burned. If they die after it is offered, the leftovers are eaten, since the מנחה already atoned for the doubt.

steps.title: The punch line: if the witnesses are found to be זוממין, the מנחה becomes ordinary
steps.stepSummary: If witnesses say she sinned, her מנחה is burned. If those witnesses are found to be זוממין, her מנחה becomes חולין. This seems to contradict רב פפא, who said the רבנן never let a sanctified מנחה go back to being ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If witnesses came and said she is defiled, her meal-offering is burned. If her witnesses were found to be זוממין, her meal-offering is ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line רב מרי was building up to. The ברייתא says that if the witnesses turn out to be זוממין, the מנחה becomes חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness case says the מנחה is burned, not redeemed, so it must already have been made holy in a כלי. Yet when the witnesses are proven false, the same מנחה becomes חולין. That is exactly the 'leaving a כלי שרת and becoming ordinary' that רב פפא said the רבנן worried about, and here nobody seems to worry about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven false because other witnesses show they were somewhere else at the time
Ordinary, not holy
Defiled, meaning she really sinned and is forbidden to her husband

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says a סוטה's מנחה becomes חולין if her witnesses are זוממין, even though it seems to have been in a כלי שרת already. That clashes with רב פפא's reason for why the רבנן kept it holy.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the witnesses who said she sinned; there the מנחה is burned, which fits רב פפא. The problem is the next case, where those witnesses are proven false and the מנחה goes back to being ordinary.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer the גמרא gives next will have to explain why the worry about things leaving a כלי שרת does not apply here.

phrases.english: If witnesses came about her that she is defiled
her meal-offering is burned.
phrases.notes: Burned, not redeemed, which tells us the מנחה was already made holy in a vessel.

phrases.english: If her witnesses were found to be lying witnesses
her meal-offering is ordinary.
phrases.notes: This is the line that bothers רב פפא: a holy מנחה turns ordinary after being in a כלי שרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and brings the actual difficulty against רב פפא's answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that the רבנן made the מנחה holy so people will not think things can leave a כלי שרת and become ordinary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the זוממין case, a מנחה that was already in a כלי שרת becomes חולין. So the ברייתא does not seem to share the worry רב פפא relied on.

steps.title: False witnesses are publicly known, so there is no confusion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12. When witnesses are proven to be עדים זוממין, everyone hears about it, so people know the מנחה was only made holy by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are bringing a proof from עדים זוממין?! עדים זוממין make a lot of noise. Everyone hears about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge against רב פפא. It says the case of עדים זוממין is not comparable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the רבנן made the מנחה holy so people would not think holy things can become ordinary. With עדים זוממין, the whole story becomes public, so everyone knows the מנחה was made holy by mistake. Nobody will learn the wrong lesson, so the רבנן had no need to keep it holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven false because other witnesses show they were somewhere else at the time
"They have a voice": the matter becomes publicly known

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב פפא's rule. The רבנן only made a rule to stop a mistaken impression, and where there is no risk of that impression, the rule does not apply.

phrases.english: You are talking about false witnesses?!
False witnesses have a voice. Their case becomes public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 and defends רב פפא's answer from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: publicity removes the reason for the rabbinic rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of עדים זוממין shows that a sanctified מנחה can go back to being חולין, which goes against רב פפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because עדים זוממין become public knowledge, nobody will think holy things can become ordinary, so the רבנן did not need to keep the מנחה holy.

steps.title: A ברייתא agrees with רב ששת for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports רב ששת's ruling about a סוטה who has witnesses overseas, but the ברייתא bases it on a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רב ששת, but not for his reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It is about to bring a ברייתא that supports רב ששת's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the דף, רב ששת ruled that if there are witnesses overseas who know she sinned, the bitter water does not test her. The ברייתא agrees with that result, but it learns it from a word in the פסוק rather than from רב ששת's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him
But not because of his reason
The אמורא whose ruling about witnesses overseas is being supported

steps.confusionAlert: "Like רב ששת, but not for his reason" means the ברייתא agrees with his result only. Do not mix up the ברייתא's source, which is a word in the פסוק, with רב ששת's own logic.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רב ששת,
phrases.notes: This goes back to רב ששת's ruling earlier on the דף: if there are witnesses overseas, the water does not test her.

phrases.english: but not because of his reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת, וְלָאו מִטַּעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The challenge to רב ששת from the burned מנחה has been answered (רב יהודה, and רב פפא as defended in step 13). Now the גמרא brings positive support for רב ששת's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that the water does not test a סוטה who has witnesses overseas
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining the word טהורה in במדבר 5:28

steps.title: The word טהורה excludes a woman with witnesses overseas
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word טהורה that the blessing of children is only for a woman who survived because she was truly pure. It is not for a woman who survived because there are witnesses overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Clean": this means truly pure, and not a woman who has witnesses in a faraway country.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main proof for רב ששת. The word טהורה shows that a woman with witnesses overseas is not cleared by the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that a woman who comes out טהורה will have children. The ברייתא says this only applies when she really is pure. If witnesses overseas know she sinned, her surviving the water proves nothing, and she does not get the blessing. That matches רב ששת's result.

keyTerms.meaning: Clean, pure: the woman is truly innocent
"A country across the sea": a faraway place

phrases.english: "Clean":

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם.
phrases.english: and not a woman who has witnesses in a country overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״טְהוֹרָה״ — וְלֹא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual words of the ברייתא that step 14 introduced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word טהורה in במדבר 5:28 limits the blessing to a woman who is really pure.

steps.title: The extra ו excludes a woman whose merit delayed her punishment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns a second case from the extra letter ו in וטהורה. A woman who survived only because a זכות put off her punishment does not get the blessing either.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And clean": this means truly pure, and not a woman whose merit held back her punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and learns a second rule from the same word. It adds another woman who survives the water but is not truly cleared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ו in וטהורה adds another case. Sometimes a woman who sinned does not die right away, because a זכות delays her punishment. Since she is not really pure, she also does not get the promised blessing of children.

keyTerms.meaning: "And clean": the extra ו teaches an additional case
Her merit held back her punishment for a while

steps.whatToRemember: The blessing of children only comes when the woman survives the water because she is truly pure. Surviving because of witnesses overseas, or because a זכות delayed her punishment, does not count.

phrases.english: "And clean":
phrases.notes: The ברייתא learns something new from the extra letter ו at the start of the word.

phrases.english: and not a woman whose merit held back her punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second teaching from the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה who survives the water only because a זכות delayed her punishment does not get the blessing of children.

steps.title: The word 'she' excludes a woman whose sin is public gossip
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns a third case from the word היא. A woman whose sin is already being talked about openly by the spinning women in the moonlight is also left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'she' teaches: not a woman about whom the women spinning thread in the moonlight are talking.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its list. It learns one more case from the word היא in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 used טהורה to leave out a woman saved by witnesses overseas. Step 16 used the extra ו to leave out a woman saved by זכות. Now היא leaves out a third woman, one whose sin is already common gossip, so the town already knows about it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'She'. A word in the פסוק that the ברייתא uses to teach a new case.
Literally 'take and give'. Here it means to talk about and discuss something.
Women who spin thread.
The moon. Here, the moonlight the women spin by.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns three cases from three parts of the פסוק: טהורה (witnesses overseas), the extra ו (זכות), and היא (public gossip).

phrases.english: "She": but not where people talk about her
phrases.notes: This is the next word in the same פסוק, וטהורה היא (במדבר 5:28).

phrases.english: the women spinning thread in the moonlight.
phrases.notes: Women sat together spinning at night and chatted about town news. If they are talking about her sin, it is already common knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הִיא״ — וְלֹא שֶׁיִּשְׂאוּ וְיִתְּנוּ בָּהּ מוֹזְרוֹת בַּלְּבָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third and last case to the ברייתא's list from steps 15 and 16.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's list of women who survive the water but do not get its blessing, part of the support for רב ששת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word היא in the פסוק (במדבר 5:28).

steps.title: A challenge to רבי שמעון begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון. Even if he does not learn anything from the extra ו, it starts to point out that there is still another case to deal with. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון: granted that he does not learn anything from the ו, but there is still...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבי שמעון. The full question finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that זכות does not delay a סוטה's punishment, so he has no reason to learn that case from the extra ו. The גמרא accepts this for now ('granted'). But its words 'there is still' show it is about to bring another case that seems to cause the same problem anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that זכות does not delay the punishment of a סוטה.
'Granted that'. Accepts one point before raising a problem.
The letter ו, here the extra letter in וטהורה.
Learns something out from a word or letter in the פסוק.
'But there is still'. Introduces a fact that creates a difficulty.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. Do not try to guess the whole challenge yet. Only the opening, 'granted... but there is still', appears on this amud.

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון,
granted that he does not learn anything from the ו,
phrases.notes: This is the extra ו in וטהורה from step 16. רבי שמעון holds זכות doesn't delay her punishment, so he doesn't need it.

phrases.english: but there is still

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, נְהִי דְּוָיו לָא דָּרֵישׁ, וְהָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's cases to start questioning רבי שמעון's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that זכות does not delay the punishment of a סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without the ו, another case (finished on the next amud) seems to cause the same problem that rejecting זכות was meant to avoid.
